pins.title: Windy night? Angle your tent stakes.
pins.sub: About 45°, leaning away from the tent.
pins.pinTitle: How to stake a tent in wind: drive stakes at about 45 degrees, top leaning away from the tent
pins.description: Stakes pushed in straight up pull out easily when the wind loads the guylines. Drive each one in at about 45 degrees with the top leaning away from the tent, so the line pulls across the stake, and push it in nearly to the hook. Our pack of 10 aluminum tent stakes, 7 in (18 cm) with hooked tops, replaces the bent and lost ones. Gear ships in 6-13 business days.

pins.title: Bottle lid frozen shut?
pins.pinTitle: Winter hiking tip: stop your water bottle lid freezing shut by carrying the bottle upside down
pins.description: Water in a bottle freezes from the top down, so the lid and threads ice up first. Close the lid tight, carry the bottle upside down in an insulated sleeve or inside your pack, and start with warm water. Our printable Winter Hiking Guide & Cold-Weather Checklist covers water, layers, traction and when to turn back. Instant PDF download.

pins.title: Hiking at 60°F? Dress like this.
pins.sub: Light layers you can tie on.
pins.pinTitle: What to wear hiking in 60 degree weather: a light long-sleeve, breathable pants and a layer to carry
pins.description: 60°F (about 16°C) feels warm on a sunny climb and cool in the shade or wind. Start with a light, quick-drying long-sleeve top and breathable hiking pants, and carry a thin jacket or fleece for breaks and the summit. Skip cotton. Our full guide to what to wear at 60 degrees.

pins.title: Hunting season? Wear blaze orange.
pins.pinTitle: Hiking during hunting season: wear blaze orange and check your state wildlife agency for dates
pins.description: Late fall is deer season in many states, and plenty of trails cross land open to hunting. Wear a blaze orange hat and vest, put orange on your dog too, stay on the trail and check your state wildlife agency for season dates and closed areas. Our guide to hiking safely in hunting season.

pins.title: A family walk before the big meal
pins.sub: Pick a short, easy trail nearby.
pins.pinTitle: Thanksgiving morning hike: how to choose an easy, short trail for the whole family
pins.description: A morning walk before the feast works best on a short, flat trail close to home: check the distance and elevation gain, pick a loop with a turnaround point, and dress everyone warm for a frosty start. In hunting season wear blaze orange. Our beginner guide to choosing your first trail.

pins.title: Snowy city day? Warm feet anyway.
pins.pinTitle: Warm merino wool socks for winter in the city: cushioned crew socks for snowy commutes and errands
pins.description: Slush, cold benches and long waits at the bus stop: cushioned crew socks with 80% merino wool keep feet warm and dry inside winter boots, and stay fresh all day. For the city, work, travel and the trail. Two sizes, four colors..

pins.title: Cabin weekend, cozy feet
pins.pinTitle: Cozy merino wool socks for a winter cabin weekend: soft, warm cushioned crew socks
pins.description: Cold cabin floors, a fire and a mug of coffee: our cushioned crew socks are 80% merino wool, soft enough to live in all weekend and warm enough for the snowy walk outside. Two sizes (about US men's 4-11 / women's 6-12), four colors.

pins.title: Thirsty dog on the trail?
pins.sub: A bottle with its own bowl.
pins.pinTitle: Dog water bottle with bowl for hiking: press to fill, unused water goes back in the bottle
pins.description: Pouring water into your hand wastes most of it. This dog water bottle has its own drinking bowl: press the button to fill it, and what your dog leaves flows back into the bottle. Lock button for the bag, wrist strap, 350 ml (11.8 oz) or 550 ml (18.6 oz), six colors. Gear ships in 6-13 business days.

pins.title: Kids bored at mile one?
pins.pinTitle: Kids nature scavenger hunt printable: hiking activities and trail bingo for family hikes
pins.description: Turn a family walk into a game: printable nature scavenger hunts, trail bingo and a junior hiker journal that keep kids looking, counting and walking. Great for holiday-week walks with the family. Instant PDF download.

pins.title: Chasing summits next year?
pins.pinTitle: Peak bagger logbook printable: Colorado 14ers, New Hampshire 4,000-footers and Adirondack High Peaks checklists
pins.description: Working on the Colorado 14ers, the New Hampshire 4,000-footers or the Adirondack 46? A printable peak bagger's logbook with a checklist for each list, so every summit gets ticked off. A good gift for the peak chaser in your life. Instant PDF download.
